fieldMarks: Grayish-brown or buff coat, lighter belly, black on upper side of tail
Sides of the head light brown with gray; lighter contour around the eyes
behavior: Active roughly April-August, dormant the rest of the year
Lives in large colonies but keeps distance from neighbours
Six call types: chirp, churr, squeal, squawk, teeth-clatter and growl
Eats green vegetation and seeds; some invertebrates and vertebrates
habitat: Dry meadows, pastures and cultivated fields in high valleys and montane grassland and shrub-steppe nearly to timberline, at 1,219-2,438 m; burrows in loose soil.
range: Southern Montana, southeastern Idaho, western Wyoming and north-central Utah.
